newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire's Mobutu boards peace talks ship.
newsitem.headline: Zaire's Mobutu boards peace talks ship.

text.p: Zaire's President Mobutu Sese Seko boarded a South African naval ship on Friday for talks with rebel leader Laurent Kabila hosted by South African President Nelson Mandela, witnesses said.

The veteran leader, who had been unable to climb 31 steep steps to board the SAS Outeniqua for health reasons, was driven up a make-shift ramp in a bullet-proof limousine around five hours behind schedule, the witnesses added.

Mobutu, who is suffering from cancer and arrived in Congo's port of Pointe Noire by plane from Kinshasa earlier in the day, smiled through the window of the car. Wearing his trade-mark leopard-skin hat, he waved at onlookers.

He drove in a motorcade of about 20 cars to the ship, which was moored in Pointe Noire. Two of the cars drove on board the ship. He made no comment on emerging from the car, accompanied by more than a dozen aides and bodyguards.

South African officials said the ship would steam for two hours for a planned rendezvous with Kabila in international waters off Angola. Some sources close to the talks suggested that because of the delay Kabila would join the ship by helicopter sooner.
